findings.title: Some screen-only passages have no highlighted target
findings.problem: The playback hook handles a failed voice check by activating the segment and displaying "Read this part on screen." However, App.jsx never maps the "instruction" or "correction" segment IDs to highlighted elements. The correct-order and correct-cloze-choice paragraphs lack ra(fbReader, "correction", ...), and the case feedback verdict likewise lacks its reader mapping.
findings.failure_scenario: An ordering question's correction fails both voice checks while its verdict and rationale pass. Playback goes silent for the correction and tells the student to read the indicated part, but nothing identifies the correct-order paragraph. The fallback does not provide the promised follow-along behavior for the actual correction.
findings.fix: Give every potentially silent segment a visible target, including instructions, corrections, and case verdicts. Add an integration test that returns 422 for a correction and verifies that the corresponding rendered answer paragraph is highlighted during the silent interval.

findings.title: Queue pagination defeats fresh-before-retry prioritization
findings.problem: drainQueue reads only the oldest 1,000 entries and then sorts that subset by attempt count. Fresh requests outside that first page are invisible, so retried passages are processed ahead of fresh ones despite the documented priority. The admission limit permits 4,000 items per day, each potentially producing several queue entries, so this boundary is reachable.
findings.failure_scenario: The oldest 1,000 entries are retries from an earlier outage, and a new student's passages are entries 1,001 onward. Even after the provider recovers, every run selects old retries before the fresh request; the fresh-first sort never sees that request until older entries have been removed.
findings.fix: Select work across the complete queue using the intended priority, either through pagination followed by global selection or a queue representation that supports priority-aware retrieval. Add a regression test with more than 1,000 entries and fresh work beyond the first page.

findings.title: Prewarming retries a failing passage indefinitely
findings.problem: The MAX_ATTEMPTS retry limit is implemented only in drainQueue. In prewarmBank, a transient synthesis or transcription failure returns immediately without persisting an attempt count or advancing the cursor. The next scheduled run pays for the same passage again, indefinitely across daily budget resets. This contradicts the worker's documented per-passage retry bound and its claim that failures do not block progress.
findings.failure_scenario: A bank passage consistently produces a provider 500 or a transcription failure. Every scheduled prewarm run retries that passage, spending again and preventing all later bank items from being prewarmed. No give-up record is produced after five attempts.
findings.fix: Persist retry state for prewarmed passages and apply the same bounded-attempt policy used for queued work. Once the limit is reached, save a reconsiderable rejection record and allow the cursor to progress, while preserving the operational-failure signal. Test repeated prewarm failures beyond MAX_ATTEMPTS and verify both bounded spending and eventual progress.

assessment: Not ready to merge. The read-aloud implementation has concrete gaps in fallback highlighting, queue prioritization, and bounded retries. This review is based on the supplied diffs; tests were not executed.
